title: Ang 880–884: the third and fourth Gurus
tomorrow: who calls God Ram, who calls God Khuda, and what does the Guru say?

segments.voice: Yesterday, ang 876: Guru Nanak opened Ramkali, the calm raga. Today the same raga passes into new hands.

Third time this week, the draft comes back with one note: start over. That's usually where people quit. There's an old story that begins at exactly that point. Tradition tells it of Guru Amar Das, the third Guru, choosing who would come after him. He asks the men of his household to build him a platform. They build one. He looks at it and says: tear it down, build it again. They do. Down again. One by one the builders get annoyed and walk away. One keeps going: Jetha, the Guru's son-in-law, a man known for serving in the langar. Down, and up again. So what does Jetha say when it's knocked over one more time?
screen: `START OVER. AGAIN.` → `BUILD IT, TEAR IT DOWN.` → `ONE BUILDER STAYS.`

segments.voice: In the telling, Jetha folds his hands and says something like: forgive me, I keep getting it wrong; show me once more. Tradition says that's when Guru Amar Das knew. Jetha became Guru Ram Das, the fourth Guru. Whether every brick of the story happened, nobody can check; it's a sakhi, a story told for what it teaches. But the handover itself is right there on the page. Open to ang 880 in Ramkali. The hymns are headed Mahala 3: the third Guru's. Guru Amar Das begins with the ages of the world. In paraphrase: in the age of truth, everyone spoke truth, and devotion lived in every house through the Guru. The ages change; what carries a person through, the hymns keep saying, is the Name, received through the Guru. A little further on, the heading changes: Mahala 4. The fourth Guru. The voice changes. The signature doesn't. Both Gurus sign their hymns Nanak. That's how the Granth shows a handover: one light, passed hand to hand, and the name at the bottom stays the same. So here they are, side by side in one raga: the one who knocked the platform down, and the one who kept building it back up. Teacher and student on the same pages. Two gurus.
screen: `TRADITION TELLS IT AS A SAKHI.` · `ANG 880: MAHALA 3, THE THIRD.` · `THEN MAHALA 4, THE FOURTH.` · `BOTH SIGN AS NANAK.` · then, large: `TWO GURUS.`

segments.voice: Find a scrap of paper and write one short line by hand: a line of the Granth you know, or just the name both Gurus signed, Nanak. Then write it again underneath, slower, the way Jetha rebuilt, with nothing wrong with the first. If you'd like, read ang 881 before you begin.
Ang 880. Where Guru Amar Das sings in Ramkali, and a little further on Guru Ram Das takes up the same raga: two Gurus, one signature.
Two gurus: one knocked the platform down, one kept building, and both signed Nanak. That's today, rebuilt.
